item.description: As the FIJI Water Flying Fijians prepare to take on Japan tomorrow, Head Coach Jake White says every player aspiring to represent Fiji must earn their place and work hard to wear the white jersey. item.content:encoded:
As the FIJI Water Flying Fijians prepare to take on Japan tomorrow, Head Coach Jake White says every player aspiring to represent Fiji must earn their place and work hard to wear the white jersey.

Speaking to the media from Japan, White says their game plan for Japan is simple and when a player gets the ball, they need know what to do and how their teammates will manoeuvre around them.

He says the clash against Japan tomorrow marks the starting point of the team's Rugby World Cup journey, with 343 days remaining until the tournament.

The coach says h aving lived in Japan and coached several teams there, he understands the Japanese style of rugby and believes his players are ready for battle this weekend.

Insert White on players response 23 October ML

The Flying Fijians will play Japan at 5.50pm tomorrow in Tokyo.

item.title: Mooar puts Drua culture and relationships first
item.description: Understanding the Drua’s culture, building relationships and learning what motivates players will be the first priority for new Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar. Speaking to fijivillage News, Mooar says he wants to fit into the team’s existing culture before contributing, stressing that what has worked at other teams cannot simply be transferred to the Drua.
item.content:encoded:
Understanding the Drua’s culture, building relationships and learning what motivates players will be the first priority for new Swire Shipping Fijian Drua head coach Brad Mooar.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Mooar says he wants to fit into the team’s existing culture before contributing, stressing that what has worked at other teams cannot simply be transferred to the Drua.

Insert: Need to fit in first - Mooar Oct 23

Mooar says faith and family are central to the Drua environment, alongside rugby, and these factors must be understood when working with the players.

He says coaching is only part of his role, as developing players as people must come first.

Mooar says the priority is to grow players as individuals before developing them as athletes.

The Drua will kick off their home campaign in Round 1 on February 13th against the Highlanders at Four R Stadium in Ba , with kick-off set for 3.30pm.

Their second home game will be played on February 27th against the Reds at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, also at 3.30pm.

In Round 6, the Drua will travel to Churchill Park in Lautoka to face the Blues on March 20th, with kick-off scheduled for 3.30pm.

In Round 9, the Drua will host the Western Force at Four R Stadium in Ba on April 10th, with kick-off set for 4.30pm.

They will then welcome the Hurricanes to HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on April 30th.

In Round 14, the Drua will take on the Brumbies at Churchill Park in Lautoka on May 15th, with kick-off scheduled for 3.30pm. The following week, they will return to Suva to face the Crusaders at HFC Bank Stadium on May 21st.

The Drua’s final home game of the season will take place in Round 16 on May 29th, when they host the Waratahs at Four R Stadium in Ba. Kick-off is set for 4.30pm.

The Drua’s away games begin in Round 2 on February 20th when they face the Waratahs at Allianz Stadium in Sydney at 7.30pm.

Their second away game will be against the Brumbies on March 6 at GIO Stadium in Canberra, with kick-off at 7.30pm.

In Round 5, on March 13, they will take on the Hurricanes in Wellington at 4.30pm

According to the Drua, they will face the Reds in Round 7 on March 28 at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, with kick-off at 3.10pm and they will then play the Highlanders in Christchurch on Sunday, April 4th, at 2pm.

In Round 10, the Drua will meet the Chiefs on April 16 at FMG Stadium Waikato, with kick-off at 7.30pm and they will face the Blues at Eden Park in Auckland on May 7.

The Drua will round off their away fixtures against the Waratahs in Round 17 on June 4 in Perth, with kick-off at 8pm.

item.title: Nadroga-born debutant Peni Naruma confident ahead of Flying Fijians’ Japan Test tomorrow
item.description: The FIJI Water Flying Fijians are well prepared for tomorrow’s Test match against Japan, with Nadroga-born Nadi rugby player Peni Naruma saying the team remains focused on its goals and continues to learn from its senior players. Naruma, who is a member of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, has represented Nadi in the Skipper Cup and is now with the Flying Fijians in Japan.
item.content:encoded:
The FIJI Water Flying Fijians are well prepared for tomorrow’s Test match against Japan, with Nadroga-born Nadi rugby player Peni Naruma saying the team remains focused on its goals and continues to learn from its senior players.

Naruma, who is a member of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, has represented Nadi in the Skipper Cup and is now with the Flying Fijians in Japan.

He says preparations have been going well this week, with the team working hard ahead of the match.

Naruma says the dreams and goals of the younger players have not changed, and he has learned a lot from the senior players in the national team.

He says he is grateful for their guidance and continues to learn something new every day.

Naruma says he is also enjoying the opportunity to be part of the Fiji national team camp.

He adds that the team is well prepared for tomorrow’s Test against Japan.

Fiji will play Japan at 5.50pm tomorrow in Tokyo.

item.description: HLB Mann Judd Suva Futsal thrashed Extra Supermarket Labasa Futsal 15-0 in the Extra Futsal IDC 2026 at the Vodafone Arena in Suva. Suva Futsal dominated from the start and led 5-0 at half-time.
item.content:encoded:
HLB Mann Judd Suva Futsal thrashed Extra Supermarket Labasa Futsal 15-0 in the Extra Futsal IDC 2026 at the Vodafone Arena in Suva.

Suva Futsal dominated from the start and led 5-0 at half-time.

Suva scored another 10 goals in the second half to seal a convincing 15-0 victory over Labasa.

Meanwhile, in other matches, Tailevu Naitasiri Futsal defeated Nadi Futsal 6-2, Ba Futsal beat Rewa Futsal 6-3, while Lami Futsal defeated Rakiraki Futsal 4-2.

Looking at today's matches, Nadi Futsal will take on Ba Futsal at 2.30pm, followed by Labasa Futsal against Rakiraki Futsal at 4pm.

Tailevu Naitasiri Futsal will face Rewa Futsal at 5.30pm, while Suva Futsal will take on Lami Futsal at 7pm.

item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji Airways Men's National 7s halfback Terio Tamani will form the halves combination with fly-half Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula as new Flying Fijians coach Jake White looks to reignite the sleeping giant of Fiji Rugby when they face Japan in a Test match this Saturday.

White has named a formidable side to face the Brave Blossoms, with the assistance of his coaching staff, despite having spent only a short time with the team.

The Rugby World Cup-winning coach says players must earn their places in the team and work hard to wear the white jersey with pride.

White says he has spent just one week with the squad and is still getting to know the players.

However, he says the players have embraced everything introduced this week and there is no shortage of energy within the team.

White believes he can provide what Fiji Rugby needs and says the timing is right for him to take on the challenge of rebuilding the team and restoring its standing on the global stage.

He adds that there is plenty at stake this weekend as Fiji prepares to take on Japan's Brave Blossoms.

Fiji will play Japan at 5.50pm this Saturday in Tokyo.
